wu: Eid Memory Chain: Teacher starts with 'Eid al-Fitr is a happy time.' Each student adds one true sentence about Eid, e.g., 'We visit family,' 'We eat special food.'
wuAlt: Eid Pictionary: Teacher draws 'family gathering' or 'new clothes' for students to guess the English word.
Eid Word Association: Teacher says 'Eid', students shout related words like 'family', 'gifts', 'prayer'.
pres: Show two emails on the board: a formal one to a boss (Subject: Eid Holiday Request) and an informal one to a friend (Subject: Eid Plans!). Highlight openings (Dear Mr. Smith / Hi Fatima) and closings (Best regards / See you soon!). Ask students to spot the differences.
presAlt: Email Sorting Game: Print/email examples. Students sort them into Formal/Informal piles.
Realia Display: Show a physical Eid card vs. a printed email. Discuss which is for whom.
prac: Email Transformation: Students receive a text message like 'Can we meet for coffee after Eid?' and transform it into a formal email to a teacher. They write the greeting, body, and sign-off. Circulate to help with 'Dear' vs. 'Hi'.
pracAlt: Pair Editing: Student A writes a short informal email, Student B adds a formal closing. Swap roles.
Subject Line Game: Give students a topic (e.g., 'Eid Party Invite'). They write 3 subject lines: formal, informal, and neutral.
ls: Listen to two model emails being read aloud. Students raise a red card for formal and a blue card for informal. Check answers by asking, 'Why was the first one formal?'
re: Stand Up, Sit Down: Teacher says a phrase. Students stand if it's for a friend (e.g., 'See you later!'), sit if it's for a boss (e.g., 'Thank you for your consideration.').
prod: Pair Work: Roleplay two scenarios. 1) Student A is a boss, Student B requests Eid leave. 2) Student A is a friend, Student B invites them to an Eid dinner. Use email language from the lesson.
rw: Write a short email draft: Students choose one real-life purpose (e.g., request a day off, invite a cousin). Write 3 sentences: opening, one body sentence, closing. Teacher checks individually.
st: Read a short story, 'My Best Eid Memory,' using simple past tense (e.g., 'Last year, we visited my grandparents. They gave me gifts. We ate a big meal.'). End with 'Goodbye, and thank you for your emails today!'
g: In teams, write the best subject line for a given topic (e.g., 'Eid Gift').
Match greetings (Dear Sir) with closings (Yours faithfully).
One student writes a greeting, the next adds a body sentence, the last a closing.
Ask 3 classmates 'What is your favorite Eid food?' and write the answers.
Write a formal email to a shop about a broken gift.
diff: Fast finishers: Write a second email with two body sentences.
Support: Use a template with sentence starters like 'I would like to request...'.
hw: Write a real email draft to a teacher about a holiday.
Write a short story: My best Eid memory (3-5 sentences).
Find an example of a formal email online and bring it to class.
tip: Always connect functional language to students' real goals; in Oujda, emailing for work or study is highly relevant, so use authentic examples like leave requests.
